A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Scaf-GRPO work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, mathematical reasoning results, GPQA-Diamond evaluation and component ablations, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original stability experiments, sensitivity analyses, hint-quality assessments, repeated-sampling evaluations and continued-training results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same guidance exemption phase, incremental knowledge/planning/solution hint search, replacement of one failed trajectory and prompt-conditioned GRPO objective. The new off-policy formulation is an experimental comparator, not a revision of Scaf-GRPO.

E1.justification: Both use DeepScaleR-Preview training data and the same seven mathematics benchmarks plus GPQA-Diamond. Added backbone, hint-source, sampling and data-mixture experiments remain within this coverage; the hint-quality audit analyzes existing training material.

E2.justification: v2 retains Vanilla GRPO, SimpleRL-Zero, Oat-Zero and LUFFY, while adding evaluated comparisons with Eurus-2-7B-PRIME, rStar-Math-7B and OpenReasoner-Zero in Table 16, DAPO in Table 18, and an explicit off-policy alternative in Table 9. This substantially broadens the comparator set.

E3.justification: The original greedy pass@1 evaluation is retained. v2 adds avg@16 evaluation with temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95, graduation tracking over 300 training steps, a Gemini-2.5-Pro hint-rating protocol, additional controlled parameter sweeps and continued training from DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview. These substantially expand evaluation design without establishing changes to the original training settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds prompt-conditioning stability tests (Figure 7 and Table 9), exemption-duration and data-mixture sweeps (Tables 11–12), hint-quality/source analyses (Tables 13–14), quantitative skill-graduation tracking, computational-efficiency analysis and sampling robustness checks. These test several previously unexamined aspects of the method.

E5.justification: Appendix I newly averages binary success over 16 sampled responses per problem, adding repeated-sampling performance estimation to v1's single greedy response evaluation. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests; the addition does not establish uncertainty across training runs.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are retained, but substantial new results appear. Examples include Qwen2.5-Math-7B avg@16 averages of 48.1% for Scaf-GRPO versus 44.8% for Vanilla GRPO (Table 15), DeepScaleR continued-training averages of 59.1% versus 54.0% (Table 17), and DAPO's 48.5% versus Scaf-GRPO's 50.9% (Table 18). These are additional comparisons or conditions, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix F.5 newly formalizes the alternative ratio that conditions the current policy on the original prompt and the old policy on the hinted prompt (Equation 13), contrasting it with matched conditioning. The original objectives, algorithm and case analysis remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same learning-cliff motivation, hierarchical on-policy scaffolding proposal and broad model-applicability claims. The headline 44.3% relative AIME24 improvement is unchanged. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through explanations connecting prompt mismatch to clipping instability, selective intervention to faster convergence, and hint-quality ratings to training utility. It also argues that scaffolding enables further learning from an already-converged DeepScaleR checkpoint and distinguishes intervention from DAPO's filtering. The original limitations concerning hint preparation and verifiable tasks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds the complete hint-judging rubric and prompt, identifies Gemini-2.5-Pro, and reports training time and peak memory. It removes v1's front-page repository link and instead states that source code and scripts accompany the supplementary material; their actual availability cannot be verified from these PDFs. Existing hardware, software and main hyperparameter documentation is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for PRIME, rStar-Math and OpenReasoner-Zero, and introduces focused positioning against DAPO's filtering and alongside DeepScaleR continued training. The related-work section and central distinction from prefix-based guidance remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. There are targeted rewrites in the experimental discussion and exemption-period appendix, additional ethics/reproducibility/LLM-use statements, revised front matter and a switch to author-year citations. The scientific additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different conference layout, changing typography, title/abstract presentation and placement of retained figures and tables, including text wrapped around several displays. It also adds the clipping plot, numerous diagnostic and comparison tables, and an expanded GPQA table. The original figures are retained rather than replaced by new scientific content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method. Compared with v1's greedy evaluations and illustrative autonomy case, it adds repeated-sampling evaluation, quantitative graduation tracking, direct stability tests, sensitivity and hint-quality controls, and broader baselines. These address important gaps in evidence for robustness, mechanism and practicality. Some new prose overstates the tables—for example, Table 9's claimed universal superiority excludes its Gaokao result—and training-run uncertainty remains unreported, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
